transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um, well, I'm here because... I hope I explain this right, but for months now I’ve just been trying to get people to understand what's been going on. It’s a little embarrassing to talk about, honestly, because I don't want to sound like a difficult person. But my husband’s family has been... well, they've been quietly messing with our money and our good name. 

I know how that sounds, but I see it happening. Like, I work as a billing clerk, and these little billing errors will just suddenly show up at my work. Or someone at our church will just start acting really funny toward me out of nowhere. People try to pull up records or tell me it's just a coincidence, but no matter what they show me, I just know it ties back to his family. 

I'm just trying to protect our family, really. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you ever been shown proof that contradicts your belief about your husband's family, and if so, how did you respond to that?

Well, yes, people have tried to show me things. Like my supervisor at work, she’s very nice, and she pulled up the system logs to show me that the billing errors were just regular computer glitches. And I really don't want to be a bother to anyone, so I always just smile and thank them for taking the time. I'd hate to seem ungrateful or argumentative. 

But... well, like I was saying earlier, no matter what records anyone pulls up, I just know it ties back to them. His family is just very careful about how they do it. I usually just keep it to myself when people show me that kind of proof, because I don't want them to think badly of me or think I'm trying to start a fight. I hope that doesn't make me sound unreasonable, Doctor. I'm just trying to be completely honest with you... am I explaining that okay?
Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed things that others around you don’t seem to notice, like voices or visions?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I've never... I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm... well, you know, losing my grip on reality or anything like that. I would really hate for you to think that. 

I'm very normal, I promise. It's just the actual, real things happening around me that I notice, like I mentioned before. But no, definitely no voices or visions or anything scary like that. Is that what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
How long have you believed that your husband's family has been messing with your money and good name?

Well, um... I guess it's been about nine months now. It all sort of started around the holidays. We had some... well, just some disagreements with his family over money and, you know, expectations for the holidays. I really hate conflict, so I tried to just smooth things over, but ever since then, I've been noticing these things happening. 

I hope I'm not making them sound like terrible people, Doctor. I'm sure they think they're doing what's right for them, but it's just been going on since that trouble we had. Does that help answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
Have you ever had any other strong beliefs that others don't seem to share, even when they’ve tried to show you otherwise?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really try to be open-minded and listen to other people's perspectives. I'd never want to be the kind of person who just stubbornly refuses to see reason, you know? 

I think I'm usually pretty agreeable. I mean, besides this situation with my husband's family, I don't have any other... well, I don't hold onto things if someone shows me I'm mistaken. I'm always happy to admit when I'm wrong about something at work or with my friends. I hope that's what you were asking? I just really want to assure you that I'm generally a very reasonable person. Am I doing okay with these questions?
Have you ever experienced a time when your mood was unusually high, overly energetic, or you felt like you didn’t need much sleep?

Oh, my, no. I definitely need my sleep! Um, if I don't get a solid seven or eight hours, I'm just terrible at my job the next day. You really have to pay close attention to the numbers when you're doing billing, you know? 

So, no, I've never had a time where I felt like I didn't need to sleep, or... or felt unusually high or anything like that. I'm actually a very steady person, I think. I just have normal energy, like anyone else. I hope that's a good thing? I try very hard to keep a regular routine so I can be reliable for everyone. Is that what you needed to know? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, of course, everyone has their off days, especially when things get stressful, but I've never felt hopeless or anything drastic like that. I try to stay positive, you know? 

I still enjoy my life and my routines. I like to keep busy and make sure I'm doing a good job at work, and I still enjoy spending time at home. I'd hate for you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself, because I'm really not. I try to be a very upbeat person for the people around me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering these the way you need me to.
Have you ever had any other experiences where you believed someone or a group of people were deliberately acting against you, even if others didn't see it the same way?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. I really try to get along with everyone, I promise. Like I said, I'm usually very agreeable and I don't like conflict. 

I mean, aside from what's happening with my husband's family, I don't think anyone is out to get me or anything like that. I've always had good relationships with my coworkers and my friends. I always try to see the best in people, you know? I would never want to be one of those people who is always suspicious or paranoid about others. I really hope you don't think I'm like that? I just want to be clear that this situation with my in-laws is... well, it's very specific, and not at all how I usually am. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of who I am.
Have you ever had any beliefs that you know other people might find strange or hard to believe, even if you feel certain they are true?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... I don't think so. I'm actually a very practical person. Working in billing, you kind of have to be very literal, you know? It's all just numbers and facts. So I don't really have any strange ideas or... or wild theories about the world or anything like that. 

Just the usual things, really. I believe in working hard and being a good person. I hope that doesn't make me sound too boring! But no, I don't have any beliefs that people would find hard to believe. I really try to stay very down-to-earth. Did I answer that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
